name: issue-driven-development
description: IDD methodology marketplace: issue-driven workflow for AI-assisted development. Every change starts with an issue, every issue is diagnosed before implementation, every implementation is scope-controlled, every completion is independently verified, every closure is documented.

plugins.name: issue-driven-dev
plugins.description: v3.0.0 (BREAKING): the closing-summary helper may VETO and may never PERMIT. After twelve verify rounds failing in one direction — a real summary the recogniser could not follow classified `missing`, and `missing` being the sole authorisation for `/idd-close --retroactive` to post a duplicate — the power was split along the direction that is sound. "A marker IS here" is an observation; "a marker is NOT here" is an inference from a failure to recognise, and no matcher over source bytes can answer a question about rendered output in the negative. Gate exit codes are now 1 (recognised) / 2 (undeterminable) / 10 (nothing recognised — NOT permission); there is no exit 0 in gate mode, deliberately, so a caller still reading `rc == 0 means go` breaks loudly. Gate class `missing` → `unrecognised`, every reply carries authorises:false, and a fifth class `mentioned` names the state the tool can actually observe. `--retroactive` loses its unattended path: the skill must read the comment set itself and obtain human confirmation that cannot be disabled. Classification now asks who wrote the comment, so a commenter can no longer move an issue between classes. Also: three more exit-0 parser paths, markup counted as content three layers deep, a quotation reaching `compliant`, the mention gate passing on zero iterations by three routes, untrusted prose reaching a shell command line, and #317 criterion (c) answered correctly for the first time in five attempts. Ten guards were mutation-proven vacuous and rebuilt.

plugins.name: idd-route
plugins.description: v0.2.1: generation-neutral candidate naming (#251) — codex-xhigh; old stats records preserved as history. v0.2.0: Pin to idd-route-swift v0.3.0 — adds update-outcome (idd-close calls this to finalize merged/abandoned) and backfill (one-shot seed from past GitHub verify-comment history; uses gh CLI). The /idd-route:backfill skill now actually works (was placeholder in v0.1.0). idd-close Step 4.5 in issue-driven-dev v2.38.0+ now succeeds instead of gracefully no-op'ing on command-not-found. v0.1.0: Data-driven agent routing for IDD methodology. Recommends Codex (GPT-5.5 xhigh) vs Claude (Opus 4.7 / Sonnet 4.6 / Haiku 4.5) per IDD issue based on observed track record per (complexity, scope_class) bucket with exponential decay (recent decisions weight more, half-life 30 days). Falls back to static heuristic rubric when fewer than 5 data points exist for a candidate (cold start). Wraps the PsychQuant/idd-route-swift binary (universal arm64+x86_64), auto-downloaded via bin/idd-route-wrapper.sh on first use following the version-aware pattern from che-word-mcp. Three thin user-facing skills: /idd-route:recommend (ad-hoc lookup; the issue-driven-dev plugin's idd-diagnose calls the binary directly), /idd-route:stats (human-readable markdown summary by bucket), /idd-route:backfill (one-shot seed from past GH verify-comment history). Per-repo stats at <repo>/.claude/.idd/routing-stats.jsonl, opt-in global mirror at ~/.cache/idd-route/stats.jsonl for cross-repo learning. Opt-out via {enabled: false} in <repo>/.claude/idd-route.json. References controlled signal vocabulary (explicit_acceptance / single_handler / sibling_sweep_needed / etc) shipped in references/signal-vocabulary.md. Static heuristic rubric in references/static-heuristic.md.
